newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall in cautious pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall in cautious pre-holiday trade.

text.p: French shares fell on Wednesday after a late drop triggered by a fall on Wall Street and an easier dollar, brokers said.

They said many investors, nervous ahead of the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, squared their positions on the eve of the Ascension Day holiday on Thursday. The market will be closed on Thursday and re-open on Friday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 8.62 points or 0.33 percent at 2,643.31 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 12.5 points at 2,624.5.
Volume totalled a moderate 6.26 billion francs.
Shares in Saint-Gobain rose 0.9 percent to 789 francs.
Analysts said the company was bullish in a conference call following the announcement of a 31 percent rise in first-quarter sales.
They said they were pleased Saint-Gobain raised flat glass prices last month and intended to raise them again this year.
Retailer Casino's shares fell 1.27 percent to 272 francs after the removal of management board chairman Georges Plassat.
His departure elicited mixed reactions but the market still views Casino as a merger candidate, brokers said.

Renault shares fell 1.63 percent to 138.70 francs, losing its early gains after an appeals court ruled it should have convened its European Group works council to discuss the Vilvoorde plant closure. Renault said it will convene the works council this month and could still close the plant by July 31.
